verdicts.reason: Identical name and identical artifact list; Y only reorders the anchor examples and adds a surface-format reminder that X already implies.
Both score presence of list markers only and both explicitly exclude item content, so scores would be interchangeable.
Both score whether burden claims are grounded in concrete staffing, timing, equipment, workflow, or cost constraints, with the same 0 anchor of bare inconvenience.
Same construct with the same enumerated 10 markers and the same 5 and 0 anchors; Y is a compressed restatement of X.
Both require a named affected group, its exposure pathway, and a link to a regulatory choice, with generic public or fairness talk as 0.
X measures first-hand operational practice while Y measures emotional intensity; a calm expert filing scores high on X and low on Y.
Both score the time horizon reasoned about, with delayed, repeated, cumulative, or long-term effects at 10 and short-term assertion at 0.
Both score whether a measurable monitoring, testing, reporting, feedback, or verification check is proposed, with the same 0 anchor.
Word-for-word equivalent anchors at 10, 5, and 0 and the same instruction to score operational knowledge rather than complaint force.
Both score the concreteness of who is affected and what changes for them, explicitly excluding severity.
Both score surface campaign phrasing, slogans, metadata, or standardized calls to action against bespoke docket-specific prose.
Both score specific position-relevant figures establishing magnitude, with generic or borrowed statistics counting as 0.
Both require a particular step, assumption, figure, or table in the agency analysis to be identified and explained as defective.
Both score an explicit evaluable causal chain from action to claimed effect, with bare stance or value assertion at 0.
Both require at least two distinct named groups plus an account of how the effect differs, with undifferentiated public at 0.
Both score density of quantified or attributed authority as it appears, independent of accuracy or proper use.
Both score whether factual claims carry identifiable checkable citations versus unattributed or non-authoritative sourcing, with the same 0 anchor.
X is a surface citation-format check for CFR part and section references while Y requires a developed statutory-authority argument; either can occur without the other.
Both score comparison of alternatives with stated advantages and disadvantages and a reason the preferred option wins, with categorical conclusion at 0.
Both require pinpointing plus a reason or answer, share the 5 anchor, and both cap bare pinpointing at 4.
Both score commenter-derived compliance-cost figures with the basis stated; the name change from cost to dollar burden narrows the wording only marginally and would rarely split scores.
Both score prominence of asserted license, senior role, experience, or occupational tie to the field, without checking the credential.
Identical deletion test with identical 10, 5, and 0 anchors; X only appends a motivating sentence that changes no anchor.
Both score how fully a proposed alternative's mechanism is specified in the text; Y merely resolves the no-alternative edge case to 0 that X leaves implicit.
Both are the same surface word-presence check over the same three phrases and both forbid considering engagement.
Both score a stated first-hand personal, occupational, or local stake tied to the proposal, with no personal or geographic stake at 0.
Both score counsel-style drafting register and apparatus, with informal and nontechnical text at 0, independent of position soundness.
Both score the same list of filing and document-wrapper artifacts as a surface feature against clean native prose.
Both score whether a concrete implementable alternative design is offered; the 0 anchors of proposing nothing and only objecting pick out the same comments.
